experiments.name: dependent chain
experiments.notes: Consecutive unrolled copies form an $f0 dependency chain.

latencies.notes: Data-dependent. 11 when the input is 0, Inf or NaN; 15 when the result is exact (an even power of two such as 1.0 or 4.0); 16 for an exact result from a subnormal input; 41 for an input just above an exact power of two (1+2^-52); 54 when the reciprocal square root needs the full 52-bit mantissa (rsqrt(2.0), rsqrt(max)); 55 for that case with a subnormal input. The long path retires 4/3 mantissa bits per cycle: 15 + 3*ceil(52/4) = 54, so rsqrt costs three digit times.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: frsqrt.d $f0, $f8; frsqrt.d $f1, $f9; frsqrt.d $f2, $f10; frsqrt.d $f3, $f11; frsqrt.d $f4, $f12; frsqrt.d $f5, $f13; frsqrt.d $f6, $f14; frsqrt.d $f7, $f15
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --init 'li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f8, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f9, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f10, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f11, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f12, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f13, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f14, $r4; li.d $r4, 0x3ff0000000000000; movgr2fr.d $f15, $r4' --asm 'frsqrt.d $f0, $f8; frsqrt.d $f1, $f9; frsqrt.d $f2, $f10; frsqrt.d $f3, $f11; frsqrt.d $f4, $f12; frsqrt.d $f5, $f13; frsqrt.d $f6, $f14; frsqrt.d $f7, $f15'
throughput.notes: Data-dependent. 8 independent lanes. CPI ~2.25 for special values, ~3.25 for exact squares, ~13.0 for general inputs, up to ~13.25 with maxsub. CPI is unchanged for 1-20 independent lanes; mixed fast/slow lanes are additive.

notes: Latency and throughput are data-dependent. The latency range was re-measured with unroll=100000; unroll=1000 produced values about 0.2 cycles lower because the per-call overhead was not fully amortised. Throughput is initiation-interval bound: CPI is unchanged from 1 to 20 independent lanes, and mixed fast/slow lanes are additive.
